jayi--jahee.scene: INTRODUCING JAHEE, a harbour girl who counts faster than the customs men. Late afternoon in her father's counting room at Danghang harbour on Silla's west coast. Low three-quarter angle across a low desk heaped with bamboo tally sticks and rolled paper ledgers with no visible writing: she leans in on one elbow, tapping a tally stick with a fine brush, looking up and sideways at the prince off-frame (only an out-of-focus Silla silk sleeve at the frame edge) with one eyebrow raised and a cool, unimpressed, faintly amused face: "Your sums are wrong." Behind her, through a wide open timber door, painted loosely in sea haze: a low stone quay, squat wooden grain boats with a single short mast and a woven reed-mat sail, oars stacked on deck, gulls, and the glitter of the incoming tide as warm bokeh — 7th-century Korean boats only, never tall European ships, never square-rigged masts or rope ladders. The low sun off the water rakes across her face and lilac silk from the side in soft rose-pink light (#e8a0bf), the room behind her in deep warm shadow.
